name: Startups of London

sources.title: Homepage — editorial site covering UK/London startups; nav has curated startup lists, SOL Podcast, Partners, Contact
Contact page — JS contact form (Name, Email, Subject, Message); footer lists 'Be a Guest Author' and 'Become a SOL Partner' collaboration routes

conditions: No public 'submit your startup' form exists — the free path is an editorial pitch via the /contact/ form (or podcast-guest / guest-author routes), and inclusion is at the editorial team's discretion
Coverage is scoped to London / UK startups and scale-ups; a non-UK product has no realistic fit
requirements: Editorial fit: the site curates lists like 'Startups & Scale-ups in London', 'FinTech Startups & Scaleups in London', 'AI Startups and Companies in London' — the product must plausibly belong in a UK/London startup list
Pitch via the JS contact form (requires JavaScript enabled in browser)
Alternative free routes: 'Be a Guest Author' (contribute an article) or 'Be a Podcast Guest' (SOL Podcast)
preparation: A short pitch explaining what the startup does and its London/UK connection
Which existing list/category the company fits (fintech, AI, legal tech, edtech, insurtech, health, etc.)
Founder availability if pitching a podcast-guest angle
Site URL, founding year, and headline metric that makes the inclusion worthwhile
workflow: Decide the angle: inclusion in a curated UK-startup list, a guest-authored article, or a podcast appearance
Open https://startupsoflondon.com/contact/ and submit the contact form with the pitch (JavaScript required)
If pitching list inclusion, name the specific list page the startup belongs on
Follow up via the same channel; there is no status tracker
watchFor: This is an editorial publication, not a self-serve directory — there is no guaranteed listing
The 'Register' flow on site is a Candidate/Employer jobs signup, unrelated to startup listings
Footer 'Be a Guest Author' link 404'd at research time — the contact form is the reliable route
The site is monetized with ads and pushes its own AISA product; expect slow or no replies on weak pitches
countsAsLive: The startup appears on a curated list page (e.g., /top-ai-startups-and-companies-in-london/) or a published article/podcast episode on startupsoflondon.com
unknowns: Editorial response time and whether cold pitches get answered
Whether list inclusion is ever pay-to-play (the /partners/ page exists for commercial partnerships)
Whether the guest-author program is still active (its link 404s)
